recent_posts.title: Comfy UI Crash Course For Beginners
recent_posts.summary: A beginner-friendly walkthrough of ComfyUI, a node-based interface for running Stable Diffusion models locally. Covers installation, hardware requirements (VRAM needs for SD 1.5, SDXL, and Flux), and building a basic text-to-image pipeline by connecting nodes: load checkpoint, CLIP text encoder, K-sampler, VAE decoder, and preview/save image. Explains key settings like seed, steps, CFG, sampler names, and schedulers. Also demonstrates image-to-image workflows, upscaling with 4x Ultra Sharp, fine-tunes vs. vanilla models, LoRAs, and using newer modular models like Z Image Turbo with a separate VAE and LLM-based text encoder (Qwen).

recent_posts.title: Web image formats ranked from BMP to AVIF
recent_posts.summary: A tier-list ranking of web image formats from worst to best. BMP and GIF land in D tier due to large file sizes and limitations. PNG and JPEG sit in C tier as legacy standards with decent compatibility but inferior compression. WebP earns A tier for combining transparency, animation support, and significantly better compression than JPEG. SVG also gets A tier for vector-based scalability and animation potential. AVIF takes the S tier as the modern gold standard, offering 20-30% better compression than WebP plus HDR and wide color gamut support, with ~96% browser support making it a practical default choice with WebP as fallback.

recent_posts.title: Claude Opus 4.6 vs GPT 5.4 across seven coding and UI tasks
recent_posts.summary: A hands-on comparison of Claude Opus 4.6 and GPT 5.4 across seven coding and UI tasks including SVG animation, landing page design, 3D modeling, flight simulation, stock dashboard, cloth simulation, and algorithm visualization. GPT 5.4 wins on physics simulation and code correctness, while Opus 4.6 consistently produces cleaner UI, better 3D models, and more minimal design. A practical recommendation emerges: use Opus for design decisions and GPT 5.4 for logic-heavy coding. Token usage is also compared, with GPT 5.4 on Codex consuming far less quota than Claude Code on the same $20 plan.

recent_posts.title: I am making a rogue like typing game...
recent_posts.summary: A developer shares a work-in-progress roguelike typing game inspired by Monkey Type, where players fight creatures by typing words. The demo showcases mechanics like items (quill of precision, lost hourglass), boss fights with word-flipping abilities, and a shop system. The creator details their AI-assisted workflow for generating sprite animations using ChatGPT, Gemini, and Grok (image-to-video), then extracting frames with ffmpeg. For coding, they use OpenCode with Claude Opus and GPT, noting Opus consumes far more credits than GPT for similar tasks. T3 chat is also mentioned for running parallel coding sessions.

recent_posts.title: OPENCLAW Full Tutorial From Scratch | Set up, Security & Use Cases
recent_posts.summary: A comprehensive walkthrough of setting up OpenClaw, an autonomous AI agent that runs 24/7 on a remote machine with full system access. Covers VPS setup on Hostinger, SSH hardening (disabling root login, password auth), firewall configuration with UFW, Tailscale VPN for private mesh networking, Docker container security (binding to localhost only), and practical integrations including Telegram bot setup, GitHub skill installation for automated PR creation, Cloudflare tunnels for previewing projects, voice input via Whisper, and cron jobs for daily news briefings.

recent_posts.title: Gemini 3.1 Pro vs Claude Opus 4.6 across nine real coding tasks
recent_posts.summary: A hands-on comparison of Google's Gemini 3.1 Pro vs Claude Opus 4.6 across nine real-world coding and UI generation tasks. Despite strong benchmark scores, Gemini 3.1 Pro consistently underperformed: it only won on flat visual design in the first two tests, then fell behind on 3D rendering, interactive simulations, stock tracking apps, and a circuit board toy. Key issues included tool-calling failures, incomplete feature implementation (marking sections 'coming soon'), poor environment detection (npm vs bun), and inability to one-shot complex prompts. Claude Opus completed most tasks in a single prompt with superior functionality, animations, and attention to detail.

recent_posts.title: Build a real-time AI webcam style transfer SaaS with Flux and Modal
recent_posts.summary: A walkthrough of building a real-time AI video generation SaaS app that transforms live webcam feeds into stylized video (oil painting, clay, 3D render, etc.) using the Flux 2 Klein open-source model hosted on Modal GPU infrastructure. The tutorial covers the full stack: a FastAPI WebSocket backend streaming JPEG frames to/from the model, a React frontend using canvas APIs and createImageBitmap for GPU-accelerated rendering, Clerk for authentication, and ChargeB (sponsor) for subscription billing with tiered plans. User metadata in Clerk stores subscription status and usage seconds, eliminating the need for a separate database. Video recording via CanvasCaptureStream and WebM export is also included.

recent_posts.title: AI Coding Is here to stay
recent_posts.summary: A developer shares personal reflections on how AI coding tools have reshaped software development, including killing the traditional tutorial YouTube niche. Practical tips are offered: reset context windows after 100k-200k tokens, avoid pre-made MCP/agent configs in favor of project-specific rules files, ask follow-up questions to learn from AI implementations, and run two parallel agent instances at most. The author also promotes their own React ASCII animation library (AskGen) built in under two days using Claude Opus and Codex, and teases an AI-first interactive coding learning platform.

recent_posts.title: ASCII Gen converts videos into lightweight text animations for web apps
recent_posts.summary: ASCII Gen is a new tool that converts videos and PNG sequences into pure ASCII art animations for web applications. Unlike 3D renderers or video-based solutions that add significant bundle size, this approach generates lightweight text files (around 200KB total) that can be easily integrated into React, Vue, and other frameworks. The tool provides pre-made animations, a script for custom generation, and an upcoming terminal UI for local conversion. The creator validated demand through social media before launching, getting 5,000 likes on an initial post.
